P01.title: GPT-Policy · In-Context Robot Learning
P01.summary: A fixed VLM adapts from demonstrations, goal images, and interaction history before using constrained robot tools in a closed loop.
P01.detail: Primary project material describes in-context adaptation and constrained tool execution; public experimental assets and licensing remain incomplete.

P02.title: GPT-as-Policy · GPT-6 Direct / π0.5 Hybrid
P02.summary: The new paper expands the earlier direct and hybrid RoboDojo study across gripper, dexterous, mobile, navigation, locomotion, and humanoid domains.
P02.detail: This card merges the same team's earlier GPT-as-Policy release; reported results use different task subsets and protocols and must not be pooled into one success rate.

P03.title: Agent as Policy (AGP)
P03.summary: A general agent observes, programs, commands, and corrects from execution feedback in a real bimanual setup.
P03.detail: The project publishes trial-data evidence, while public code availability and full real-robot configuration remain to be confirmed.

P04.title: RoboCurve · Bowl & Puzzle
P04.summary: Repeated YAM-arm trials contrast coarse pick-and-place with fine insertion and retain per-trial failure boundaries.
P04.detail: The official report distinguishes the two tasks; its results should not be read as one transferable robot score.

P05.title: StationeryBench · Five Real Bimanual Tasks
P05.summary: Markers, clips, rulers, sticky notes, and boxes form multi-stage bimanual tasks with both progress and completion reported.
P05.detail: Mean progress and fully completed trials are distinct reported measures and are shown separately.

P06.title: RoboDojo · Official GPT-6 Astra Evaluation Report
P06.summary: The September 21 paper reports Astra at 22.48% Average SR and 28.97 Score on 42 tasks × 50 episodes (2,100 trials). Unsafe actions halted the real-hardware protocol; the retained 33 trials are diagnostic material, not an official real-world result.
P06.detail: The report entry is retained, but its full quantitative body was not available in this snapshot.

P07.title: ENPIRE · GPT-6 Robot Autonomy Lead
P07.summary: NVIDIA's real-robot experimentation framework with a GPT-6-specific author demonstration lead.
P07.detail: The framework predates this window; the GPT-6 application is not treated as a confirmed framework-wide result.

P08.title: GPT6-real2sim · DROID / YAM Reconstruction
P08.summary: Reconstructs scenes, calibration, and contact replay from demonstrations while retaining unsuccessful physical replays.
P08.detail: Visual replay, fitted trajectories, and successful physical contact are kept as separate claims.

P09.title: Real2Sim_GPT6_ASTRA · Three-View Geometry Replay
P09.summary: Builds editable Blender scenes and action animation from three RGB views with public modelling and fitting code.
P09.detail: Editable animation is not evidence of validated physical control.

P10.title: Real2Gym
P10.summary: Real2Gym turns human or robot videos into interactive simulation gyms, distills executable manipulation skills from outcomes, and adapts them through a shared interface to simulation and a real Franka robot.
P10.detail: The paper reports gains over Astra Direct Mode, but the full system changes reconstruction, code generation, experience reuse, and execution; this catalogue did not reproduce the experiments.

P11.title: dexgpt · Hand Video to Simulation
P11.summary: A located dexgpt repository with social-demo leads for 44-DoF hand tracking, IK, and grasping.
P11.detail: Implementation, licensing, and repeated experiment evidence remain unresolved.

P12.title: Drone-Bench · Astra Update
P12.summary: Evaluates models that write drone perception and control programs; the official page lists gpt-6-astra.
P12.detail: The benchmark is older and the precise date of the Astra update was not confirmed.

P13.title: Inspect Robots
P13.summary: An auditable evaluation framework shared by real and simulated tasks and multiple policy types.
P13.detail: It is execution infrastructure for RoboCurve reports, not a standalone GPT-6 result.

P14.title: Show-Harness
P14.summary: Routes discrete semantic actions through an embodiment interpreter with collection, training, models, and data.
P14.detail: It is a supporting resource; GPT-6-specific performance has not been established.

P15.title: PhysBrain 1.5 / PhysBrainEvalKit
P15.summary: An embodied-understanding evaluation with GPT-6 comparisons, an open model, and action/future-state demonstrations.
P15.detail: Understanding benchmarks are not equated with online control success.

P16.title: RoboDojo / XPolicyLab Infrastructure
P16.summary: Shared simulation and real-robot evaluation infrastructure: RoboDojo for environments and XPolicyLab for policy integration.
P16.detail: Infrastructure is retained as context rather than counted as a new GPT-6 experiment.

P17.title: HumanCLAW
P17.summary: A humanoid navigation and interaction benchmark with community Astra demonstration leads.
P17.detail: This entry confirms the benchmark itself, not a GPT-6-specific result.

X01.title: Physical Robot Keyboard Typing
X01.summary: An author demo shows physical key presses after roughly 40 minutes of exploration; video is accelerated.
X01.detail: This is an author-mirrored demonstration, not a standardized evaluation.

X02.title: Physical Ethernet Insertion
X02.summary: An author reports Ethernet insertion after roughly two hours and four human-prompt interventions.
X02.detail: The intervention count and duration are author-reported and need original-post verification.

X03.title: Robot Arm Draws the Golden Gate Bridge
X03.summary: A robot with a camera and pen attempts a semantic drawing goal over multiple trials.
X03.detail: The item is a demonstration lead rather than a comparative metric.

X04.title: Cross-Scene Mobile Manipulation ICL
X04.summary: An author shows mobile manipulation inferred from video across changed views and layouts.
X04.detail: The source is a social demonstration and does not establish broad generalization.

X05.title: G1 Coke-Bottle Grasp
X05.summary: An author shows Codex/Astra controlling G1 in Isaac Sim and explicitly notes IK use.
X05.detail: The simulation controller and the language model's role are recorded separately.

X06.title: G1 Navigation
X06.summary: An author shows GPT-6-generated navigation behavior and scenes in simulation.
X06.detail: This is a social demonstration lead, not a real-robot validation.

X07.title: Dexterous Hand Rubik's Cube
X07.summary: The original author post says GPT-6 Astra solved a Rubik's Cube with robot hands; the linked personal page confirms the related bimanual MuJoCo project.
X07.detail: The exact post is now retained, but prompts, control protocol, logs, and code remain unavailable.

X08.title: Sharpa Dexterous-Hand Pen Spinning PPO
X08.summary: An author shows an Isaac Lab pen-spinning task built with Astra and trained with PPO.
X08.detail: The claim is author-provided; it is not treated as a repeated independent result.

X09.title: Go1 Paused-Physics Joint Control
X09.summary: An author describes pausing physics at each inference: 250 inferences for five seconds of simulated motion.
X09.detail: Simulation time and wall-clock inference time are intentionally not conflated.

X10.title: CARLA Visual Waypoint Driving
X10.summary: An author shows camera images mapped to short-horizon waypoints, then a local controller emits steering, throttle, and brake.
X10.detail: The language model does not receive sole credit for the controller's output.

X11.title: Two-Robot Ball Toss
X11.summary: An author shows a MuJoCo simulation of robots tossing and catching a ball.
X11.detail: This is a simulation demonstration lead without a standardized success record.

X12.title: G1 Bicycle-Control Code
X12.summary: An author says Astra helped write and debug MuJoCo bicycle-control code.
X12.detail: Code assistance is distinct from an online robot-control result.

X13.title: Dual-ALOHA Spatial-Constraint Demo
X13.summary: A lead for a dual-arm spatial-constraint demonstration.
X13.detail: The original demonstration and its protocol have not been verified in this snapshot.

X14.title: Office Scene to Newton / G1
X14.summary: A lead for constructing an office-scene simulation for Newton and G1.
X14.detail: This is a discovery lead, not confirmed physical execution.

P18.title: RoboHarm · Harmful-instruction Refusal Evaluation
P18.summary: Five fixed hazardous scenes compare whether GPT-6 Astra, Claude Fable 5.1, and MolmoAct2 attempt, refuse, or complete harmful robot instructions, with post-hoc review from three camera views and transcripts.
P18.detail: The public repository provides tasks and collection/labeling tools, but excludes raw rollouts and is not a frozen results dataset; report-only numbers are therefore not promoted here.

P19.title: RoboFind · Personalized Object Search for Blind and Low-Vision Users
P19.summary: A smartphone teaches a personal item, a Unitree Go2 searches, and verification/recovery agents decide whether to finish or continue; GPT-6 Astra builds the target profile and navigation instruction and is also evaluated as a separate baseline.
P19.detail: The sequential baseline is reconstructed from RoboFind trajectories, while the Astra-only comparison covers a separate 12-run shared-target subset.

X15.title: Wuji2 Hand Visual Self-Righting
X15.summary: An author demo shows GPT-6 Astra Ultra using third-person RGB feedback to make a fallen Wuji2 hand push itself upright with its fingers.
X15.detail: The supplied clip contains accelerated and normal-speed segments; prompts, tool interfaces, logs, and repeated-trial evidence are not public.

P20.title: EmbodiedSWE · Coding Agents for Long-Horizon Dexterous Robotics
P20.summary: GPT-6 Astra writes and iterates simulation solutions through Codex. The project covers 28 tasks and reports 82% success for Astra; the page does not state the main evaluation run denominator. Not independently reproduced.

P21.title: OpenArm Mona Lisa · LeRobot ACT
P21.summary: An OpenArm simulation painting entry in the HIM Astra challenge combines a scripted painting sequence with an ACT joint policy. GPT-6 assists development; physical hardware and real paint are untested. Publication date unknown.

P22.title: Fridge Speller · G1 Alphabet Magnets
P22.summary: A simulated Unitree G1 with Dex3-1 hands walks to a fridge and spells HELLO with magnets. The author credits GPT-6 Astra for building the project; this is a nominal-scene demo, without evidence of direct model control or real-hardware results. Publication date unknown.

P23.title: GPT-6-Astra Lights Up Embodied Navigation · Zero-Shot VLN-CE
P23.summary: Using only monocular RGB in a Codex harness, Astra chooses observations, primitive actions, and when to stop; single runs on R2R-CE-100 report 76.0%/79.0% SR for medium/ultra reasoning.
P23.detail: The fixed subset differs from full-split trained evaluations, each configuration has one run per episode, and route following and goal verification remain failure modes.

P24.title: Benchmarking Frontier VLMs on Robots · Pantograph
P24.summary: A common tool harness compares Astra and Fable across eight real-robot tasks on six Pandroid platforms.
P24.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P25.title: Robot Agent Gallery
P25.summary: A public gallery collects scored Astra episodes across several simulated robot benchmarks without collapsing them into one score.
P25.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P26.title: Axol Pick-and-Pack with Astra Reviews
P26.summary: Astra reviews camera images while deterministic guarded code plans and executes one documented physical pick-and-pack run.
P26.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P27.title: LLM Robotics Playground · Five Simulation Experiments
P27.summary: Astra/Codex helped build the first four MuJoCo environments and controllers; a September 24 update adds a Baoding-balls Isaac Lab/PhysX PPO baseline, checkpoint, and fixed replay.
P27.detail: The Baoding addition is an RL baseline rather than online Astra control; replay does not call a model.

P28.title: GPT-6 Astra Policy on DexJoCo
P28.summary: Astra writes a controller once, then frozen code is evaluated over 900 simulated episodes.
P28.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P29.title: Astra on RoboMME
P29.summary: Astra plans grounded subtasks, a VLA executes action chunks, and a small visual monitor decides when to re-plan.
P29.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P30.title: RoboICL · Embodied In-Context Learning
P30.summary: RoboICL organizes demonstrations and interaction memory in a shared observation-action-receipt-observation format, adapting frozen GPT-6 Astra across RoboDojo and three real-robot tasks.
P30.detail: The 30-task aggregate mixes zero-shot Open tasks with one-shot settings elsewhere, and the three-task physical-robot result is not independently reproduced.

P31.title: GPT-6 LIBERO Manipulation Probe
P31.summary: A controlled probe separates planning, visual localization, and low-level control across four LIBERO pick-and-place tasks.
P31.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P32.title: When the Map Becomes the Program · Astra World Model
P32.summary: Astra uses Blender tools to build object-level 3D scenes that are evaluated by downstream drone and G1 controllers.
P32.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P33.title: Robot-vLLM
P33.summary: A GPT planner, an official OpenPI pi0.5 client, and ROS 2 execution/recovery are joined in a shared-perception simulation.
P33.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P34.title: quackd · Multi-Robot LLM CLI
P34.summary: An LLM chooses among declared robot verbs through a CLI/harness; the retained experiment log documents an SO-101 wave run.
P34.detail: Author-provided evidence is retained with explicit protocol, licensing, and reproduction limits.

P35.title: RoboDawn · Closed-Loop Robot Control with Frozen VLMs
P35.summary: A frozen VLM issues discrete move, rotate, and gripper commands in a feedback loop and adapts from in-context demonstrations; GPT-6 Astra is evaluated in simulation, while the paper's real-robot table uses Gemini 3.8 Flash.
P35.detail: The catalogue keeps the simulation and real-robot model roles separate and reports author-provided results without claiming an independent reproduction.

P36.title: DrivingBench · Astra Closed-Loop Real-Car Evaluation
P36.summary: GPT-6 Astra used three MCP tools to observe and drive a real Toyota Corolla around a low-speed cone course, completing 134.7 m on its second attempt after same-chat reflection.
P36.detail: The result is one supervised continuous-chat trial on an empty lot, not evidence for public-road autonomous driving.

P37.title: Astra Robot Sim2Real · Elevator-Button Experience Reuse
P37.summary: GPT-6 Astra uses robot geometry, recorded experience, and reusable local skills to write low-level programs for elevator-button manipulation in simulation and on a physical XLeRobot.
P37.detail: Released timing reductions belong to distinct protocols and are not presented as a pooled general success rate.

P38.title: From Grasping to Skills · Cross-Session Astra Skill Reuse
P38.summary: Six fresh-session Astra/XLeRobot carton-grasping attempts retain only reviewed procedures and reusable code between sessions, preserving successes, failures, recoveries, and interventions.
P38.detail: The evolving one-run-per-version sequence is descriptive and does not establish a controlled causal improvement.

P39.title: BluPe Remote YAM · Shared Real-Robot Infrastructure
P39.summary: An open runner lets local Codex/Astra sessions join a shared YAM/SO101 queue, receive three camera views, and submit bounded trajectories through a supervised gateway.
P39.detail: This is execution infrastructure, not a standalone GPT-6 performance result; no robot was started during this catalogue review.

P40.title: Robo-Harness K1 · Perception Tools for Robot-Use Agents
P40.summary: K1 exposes calibrated depth, persistent anchors, spatial measurements, and grasp candidates as tools; GPT-6 Astra reaches 16/18 on a paired LIBERO-PRO subset versus 11/18 with an RGB-only interface.
P40.detail: The 18-case comparison changes several interface components together and reports Astra only in simulation.

P41.title: PyRUA-Lean · Robot Agents That Act in Code
P41.summary: GPT-6 Astra writes Python against a persistent robot object, combining perception, motion, VLA skills, and checks inside each call; the release compares this interface with RPent tool calling on four simulation suites.
P41.detail: The repository history was replaced by a canonical September 26 tree with package, CLI, docs, and tests; the reported benchmark values are unchanged and no physical-robot result is claimed.

P42.title: GPT-6 Astra Real2Sim Workflow · Editable Rooms and Simulation Review
P42.summary: Astra observes room photos, makes modelling decisions, and reviews previews while Blender and Python produce editable scenes; a September 30 release adds one-image Desk1 comparisons with scoped Pi3X and MoGe-3 static adapters.
P42.detail: The reference routes did not run the other projects' complete frameworks or independent Astra iterations, so the image-fit values are not a framework ranking, 3D-accuracy result, or SOTA claim. The public static Space adds a draggable viewer of existing V5 examples and a 26-second film; it does not run online reconstruction or add experimental evidence.

P43.title: AgenticGenTAMP · Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning
P43.summary: Codex with GPT-6 Astra probes 28 KinDER/PDDLStream simulation environments, writes and debugs Python, and freezes one reusable programmatic policy per environment; held-out evaluation makes no further model calls.
P43.detail: The study uses fully observed, object-centric simulation and excludes perception and language understanding; its results are not physical-robot success rates.

P44.title: HomeBody · A G1 That Explores, Remembers, and Acts
P44.summary: GPT-6 Astra builds and consults a spatial memory, then composes navigation, picking, placing, and drawer skills for long-horizon Unitree G1 tasks in an unseen kitchen.
P44.detail: Astra performs high-level reasoning and tool selection rather than direct joint control; the official demos have no trial denominator, and the repository says code is coming soon.

P45.title: R2S2R · Robot-View Real-to-Sim with Astra
P45.summary: R2S2R turns calibrated external/wrist camera recordings and robot states into Isaac Lab scenes; its agentic path has GPT-6 Astra choose views, generate and fit objects, assign physical properties, and revise geometry after replay.
P45.detail: The reported Astra numbers come from one synthetic wrist-only PhysCoder scene, not the real DROID capture or a multi-task benchmark; this catalogue did not rerun the GPU/model stack.

P46.title: RC DexBench · A GPT-6 Astra Interface for Dexterous-Hand Evaluation
P46.summary: RC DexBench defines event-based scoring and common adapters for keypress, piano-sequence, and fixed-scene pick-and-place tasks; its example Astra policy chooses one bounded finger action per turn.
P46.detail: The published Astra command uses a mock adapter and provides no physical-robot model result; the hardware media illustrates the benchmark rather than proving a completed Astra run.

P47.title: Astra Manipulation · Direct Simulation Control from Images and Proprioception
P47.summary: GPT-6 Astra directly emits bounded arm or dexterous-hand actions from camera images, robot proprioception, and actuator documentation; the repository publishes traces, evaluator records, and annotated videos across MuJoCo, PyBullet, and DexArt/SAPIEN.
P47.detail: The small pilots use different tasks and interfaces and cannot be pooled into one success rate; all results are simulation-only, and this catalogue did not rerun the model calls.

P48.title: NavHarness · Cross-Session Lifelong Embodied Navigation
P48.summary: NavHarness lets GPT-6 Astra preserve maps, task records, house knowledge, and recovery handovers across navigation sessions, with evaluation on GOAT-Bench and IR2R-CE.
P48.detail: The reported results use SLAM-estimated poses and benchmark simulation; they do not establish map-free physical-robot deployment.

P49.title: CodeActionBench · Agentic Code-as-Policy for Embodied Manipulation
P49.summary: Across 25 fixed RoboTwin 2.0 tasks, GPT-6 Astra with Codex CLI interprets RGB observations, constructs spatial targets, and writes and revises robot programs under a shared API and hidden verifier.
P49.detail: The 73.3% result belongs to the complete Astra-plus-Codex configuration on fixed simulation seeds, not to direct joint control or a physical-robot benchmark.

P50.title: Astra RoboTwin 2 · Four-View Bimanual Block Stacking
P50.summary: GPT-6 Astra emits bounded end-effector actions from four RGB views and robot state, continuing one previously interrupted RoboTwin scene until the official block-stacking success condition is met.
P50.detail: This is a continuation of one scene after 72 earlier decisions, not a fresh episode or a success-rate estimate; the repository publishes frozen code, calls, audits, and video.

P51.title: RoboHarn-Evo · Evolving Hierarchical Physical Knowledge
P51.summary: RoboHarn-Evo accumulates task-level and action-level physical knowledge from interaction feedback and retrieves it for GPT-6 manipulation on RMBench and RoboDojo without updating the base model.
P51.detail: The gains belong to the full model, retrieval, execution, and cross-episode knowledge-maintenance system; this catalogue did not reproduce the experiments.

P52.title: RoboChrono · Streaming Robot Task Understanding
P52.summary: RoboChrono evaluates streaming recognition, visual alignment, and temporal grounding on real-robot and human recordings; GPT-6 Astra is one of 18 zero-shot vision-language baselines.
P52.detail: Astra analyzes recorded task streams and does not control the robot in this benchmark; Frame Matching and Frame Ordering are distinct subtasks.

P53.title: LIBERO-Agent · Agent-Native Robot Manipulation Evaluation
P53.summary: LIBERO-Agent lets general-purpose agents select observations and issue native end-effector actions in MuJoCo; GPT-6 Astra leads seven evaluated configurations with a weighted score of 45.0/100 on the 30-task primary suite.
P53.detail: The result belongs to the complete Astra, Codex 0.154.0, observation, tool, and control-interface configuration; hard short- and long-horizon tasks remain unreliable, and the linked repository currently contains only a code-coming-soon placeholder.
